summary: Tested 10 robust threshold strategies (sym_grid, DE asym, DE+regularization, K-fold CV-DE date/row, bootstrap median, quantile grid, ensemble averaging) on iter_013's 5-seed regression OOF predictions. Evaluated each via 3 splits (forward-date, backward-date, random row).
diagnostic_finding: Per-half PnL is heterogeneous: halfA (96-107) yields 1.35x more PnL/date than halfB (108-119). The S1+S2 date-split gap (-6 PnL per 12 eval dates) is ~91% intrinsic to data, only 0.4 PnL is recoverable via better thresholding. This bounds the platform gap reduction from threshold strategies to <<1.
honest_accounting: Robust threshold strategies converge to nearly identical thresholds when fit on the full 442k (the data is well-determined). The platform gap of -17 cannot be meaningfully reduced by threshold tweaks — it's dominated by per-date PnL variation that no decision rule can bypass. Iter_014 ships as a marginal-improvement, zero-risk de-risking, but is not expected to deliver the +5 platform target.
